version: v5.0 (changelog dated 2026-10-08; says "MiniMax H3 replaces FLUX 3 (hub v13.3)", but the hub is now v13.4)
purpose: Role skill for realistic AI podcast-clip ads (two or more hosts at mics, cold-open pain line, peer referral, product as a friend's recommendation) and a solo UGC talking-to-camera variant (section 13). It runs autonomously from the Script Lab-gated conversation, through Pinterest-referenced casting, a master two-shot plus one start frame per character on GPT Image 2, locked ElevenLabs voices, a conversation master and packed stems, then MiniMax H3 2K lip-sync clips with one character per clip. It ends with a cut-and-interleave edit, burned captions, title bar, AI DRAMATIZATION tag and end card, and frame-by-frame QA with pitch, loudness and gap tables. It is built for cold Meta ads: offer, cost line, URL and a 3-word CTA on the end card, plus primary text and headlines.

phases.name: Before you start (Module 0 + hard gates + autonomy)
phases.does: Runs hub Module 0 (A1 brief, A2 research/VOC, A3 concept memo, B1 Voice Card, B2 Conviction Map), applies hub Section G gates, reads Copy Laws (Appendix M in Script Lab), sets the autonomy rule, and requires an AI DRAMATIZATION tag.
phases.gate: Script written only from Module 0 material, never from memory. The skill stops only when a brand fact is missing, the budget can't cover the whole ad, or every Pinterest route fails (line 32).
phases.human_checkpoint: None numbered. Autonomy rule (line 32): 'It does not ask the user to pick references.'
phases.tools_models: readymerce-ads-machine (Module 0, Section G), readymerce-script-lab Appendix M

phases.name: Write the conversation (Script Lab, podcast adapter 18c, C45)
phases.does: Script Lab WRITE or GRADE/FIX: belief ladder with the because test, script bible, reveal plan, 2-3 spines of about 80 words, the 10-beat podcast template, a numbered line list (L1..Ln) with speaker tags, numbers written as words with a noun between them.
phases.gate: Release at 85 or more out of 100 with no critical fail: 16 mechanical tests, a cold read by a fresh agent hearing 'Voice 1' and 'Voice 2', up to 3 rewrite loops. Length is 8 to 12 turns, 80 to 110 words, 35 to 45 s. Turns are 20 words or fewer (one turn may reach 25). The listener speaks every other turn and at least every 8 s, and no host carries more than 60% of the words. The brand line is 25 words or fewer, the payoff ends on 6 words or fewer, line 1 is the pain line (ICP clear within 3 s), and core lines are under 12 words, none over 17, grade 7.
phases.human_checkpoint: Only after 3 failed rewrite loops: 'then the user decides' (line 43).
phases.tools_models: readymerce-script-lab (WRITE/GRADE/FIX), optional Hook Lab stacks (hub C5), fresh-agent cold reader

phases.name: Casting and set brief
phases.does: One casting card per character (role, age band, gender/region, build, hair, grooming, wardrobe, energy, voice description, contrast) and one set card (room, light, mics, table, props, what is NOT in the room).
phases.gate: Characters visibly different. The voice description holds only timbre, age, gender, accent and pace, with no emotion words. The set card lists 3 to 5 real props and no logos, neon show sign or screens with text.

phases.name: Source references from Pinterest (autonomous)
phases.does: Builds 3-5 searches per character and 3 per set, pulls 15-30 image URLs each (Apify scraper, then built-in browser or Claude in Chrome, then Firecrawl site:pinterest.com), downloads them, tiles numbered contact sheets of about 12, scores each candidate and picks one, logs a reference board and imports the picks with media_import_url.
phases.gate: 8-point score (0-2 each), keep only 13 or more out of 16. Exactly one photo per character plus one backup that is never attached with it. The set photo has no people. If all three routes fail, stop and never generate people without a reference.
phases.tools_models: Apify Pinterest scraper, built-in browser / Claude in Chrome, Firecrawl, Higgsfield media_import_url

phases.name: Master two-shot (F0) and one start frame per character
phases.does: F0: a 16:9 wide frame of every character in the recreated set, made from the empty set photo plus one Pinterest photo per character, with the 'Create new, different people' line. F1/F2: a 9:16 medium close-up per character made with F0 as the only attachment (calm, neutral, gaze on the friend, hands resting). Optional product image on the table.
phases.gate: 5.4 frame QA at full size, 8 checks: same person as in the F0 crop, one image per person, F0 faces are not the Pinterest people, skin texture and five fingers, props and light match with no logos, characters look different, reads as a real small podcast, gaze and expression and hands right with room for the title bar. Retake with one fix ('Most frames pass in one to three tries'). Drift twice means using the upscaled crop from F0.
phases.tools_models: GPT Image 2 (gpt_image_2, quality high, 2k), per hub G7; GPT Image 2.5 rejected

phases.name: Frame plan F0..F2
phases.does: Table of every reference frame (F0 two-shot as reference only, F1 Host A used by every A clip, F2 Host B used by every B clip).
phases.gate: 'Two hosts means exactly three images: F0, F1, F2. Three hosts means four.' More than one start frame per person means the plan is wrong.

phases.name: Voices and the conversation master (before any video)
phases.does: Casts one ElevenLabs voice per character (library or designed), writes lines for talking with at most one low-intensity tag per line, generates beats of 2-7 lines with 4 takes each, picks takes by the checks, builds the conversation master with the line table, then cuts one packed stem per character per clip.
phases.gate: Scribe transcript word for word. Natural pauses with a spread of 0.1 s or more, never tightened. Turn gaps 0.08-0.3 s with occasional 0.1-0.2 s overlaps. About -16 LUFS. Stems use 0.8-1.0 s listening beats and about 1 s of tail, padded to a whole number of seconds between 5 and 15.
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs connector: creative_list_voices, creative_design_voice + creative_save_designed_voice, creative_generate_speech (eleven_v4 default). Method and checker/builder delegated to readymerce-animation-ads Phase 5 (vo_build2.py).

phases.name: Transcript check of the conversation master
phases.does: Transcribes the master with ElevenLabs Scribe (word timestamps) and compares it with the script for dropped, swapped or extra words, brand pronunciation, swallowed negations, cut-off last words and merged numbers.
phases.gate: 'Never generate video on a master with known wrong word.' Bad lines are regenerated on ElevenLabs, then the master and stems are rebuilt. Clip audio is never transcribed.

phases.name: Speaker map and budget preflight
phases.does: Packs each character's lines in script order into clips of 15 s or less (one character per clip, never splitting a line), folds short pull lines into other clips, and prices video plus images.
phases.gate: Every clip is 5-15 s, about 30-35 words (2-3 lines). A line over about 35 words goes back to the script. Usually 4-6 generations for two hosts, 5-8 for three. Budget = clip seconds × 2 credits per second + one retake of the longest clip + images with about 2 retakes per frame. Check the balance right before submitting.
phases.human_checkpoint: Only if the budget can't cover the ad: 'say so and agree scope first' (line 360).

phases.name: Generation prompt per clip
phases.does: H3 reference-mode prompt: realism, references by token, scene lock with hands, one continuous shot, behaviour lock, background, static camera, lip-sync block with pause times, context, line time spans with tone notes, constraints.
phases.gate: Exactly one image (the start frame) plus one audio (the packed stem). minimax_h3, 2K, 9:16, declined_preset_id. Duration = padded stem length (5-15 s). One tone phrase per line, at most 5 words, softened. No gesture words outside the behaviour lock. A laugh only where the script writes '(small laugh)'. Numbers as words.

phases.name: Generate and check every clip
phases.does: Submits all clips as one batch, builds a take sheet per clip, applies the reject list, measures pitch and runs the drift check.
phases.gate: Take sheet: a frame every 1 s plus the first and last 0.1 s, face crops at least 190 px. Reject a used line on lens look, profile, looking down or closing eyes for more than 1 s, leaving frame, gestures, smiling on a problem line, a frozen pose for more than 4 s, or drift from the start frame. Pitch within 1.5 semitones per character. Drift check in 2-second windows every 0.25 s, offset recorded per line, retake only when the drift sits inside a used word. Retake only the failing clip, with the same prompt plus one fix.
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg frame extraction, pitch and envelope analysis (tools unnamed)

phases.name: Edit the conversation (cut and interleave)
phases.does: The master is the timeline and the only audio. Cut map per line (clip, in, out, angle A or B punch-in, reaction overlay), audio-based cut points, reaction shots, per-line levelling, native crop, captions, title bar, end card, AI tag, then ffmpeg assembly.
phases.gate: In point 0.08 s before onset, out point 0.12-0.2 s after. Turn gaps 0.08-0.2 s, never over 0.35. A reaction shot of 0.8-1.5 s at least every 10 s. Loudness spread under 2 dB, then about -16 LUFS. Fades of 20-80 ms. Punch-in 112-118%. Captions of 1-3 words, clamped to their segment, no gap over 0.4 s. Title bar 8 words or fewer, 2 lines at most, about 44-50 px at 1080 wide, covering no head. End card about 3 s. AI DRAMATIZATION top-left. Output 1080x1920 at 30 fps, TP -1.5.
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg (Higgsfield sandbox or any shell), ASS subtitles, pink-noise room tone; ElevenLabs creative_generate_speech for clipped-word patches

phases.name: Hook variants (3 per ad)
phases.does: Main (cold-open line 1 + title bar A), same open with title bar B, and a later start (drop 1-2 turns, open on e.g. the aha line + title bar C), all cut from the same clips.
phases.gate: Seam test (hub L1, Script Lab test 12). A later start re-runs Script Lab tests 3, 5 to 10, 13 and 14. No line ever plays twice. No extra generations.

phases.name: Solo creator UGC variant
phases.does: One character talking to the phone in 1-3 real settings from the avatar's day: a master frame in setting 1 and one start frame per extra setting, a locked voice, stems packed per setting, jump-cut edit.
phases.gate: Script Lab UGC adapter (18d) at D30, C45 or S60, released at 85 or more. Same Pinterest, likeness, voice, gap, loudness and caption rules. Line 1 is still the cold-open pain line.

phases.name: QA before delivery (rendered file)
phases.does: Final frame sheet, final transcript, pitch table, loudness table, gap table, hook check, conversation check, read-aloud, reference and likeness audit, H3 compliance, phone-size watch, Copy Laws check.
phases.gate: Frames every 1.5 s or less plus the first and last frame of every cut. Pitch within 1.5 semitones. Loudness spread under 2 dB. Seam gaps 0.08-0.35 s. First 3 s name the ICP and the pain. Listener heard or seen every 8-10 s. No host over 60% of the words. Brand turn 25 words or fewer. Every clip H3 2K, 15 s or less. 'never deliver with a known failure and a note.'
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg, transcription, pitch and loudness analysis

phases.name: Deliverable package
phases.does: Concept memo, numbered script, casting and set cards, reference board, frames and frame plan, speaker map with voice IDs and stem map, prompts, take sheets with drift results, cut map, finished ad plus 3 hook variants, primary text and 2 headlines, Script Lab release, credits against the preflight, QA tables.
phases.gate: Primary text 80-250 words, opening with the hook line and ending with the 3-word CTA.

story_structures.name: Two-host cold-open discovery (podcast beat template, C45)
story_structures.shape: 1 A: cold-open accommodation, first person, the viewer's world named → 2 B: a short question showing she knows the pain → 3 A: escalation in the buyer's words → 4 B: the real cause in one plain picture line (aha) → 5 A: echo question or disbelief → 6 B: 'We had the same thing' + the wrong fix tried → 7 A: one-word pull ('And?') → 8 B: the fix + casual brand name + one thing it showed them (25 words max) → 9 A: pull for the result or the objection → 10 B: lived payoff, 6 words or fewer
story_structures.organic_fit: Very strong. The approved worked example is already an Albanian B2B services piece: two business owners in Tirana, a clinic owner answering WhatsApps at 11 pm, the cause 'whoever answers first gets them', then the agency (Mardyos, here in Tirana). For organic, beat 8 becomes the mechanism or insight (e.g. 'we set an auto-reply that answers in minutes and books the call') instead of 'a free session with X'. The agency is the account itself, so the brand name can drop or become a light 'our team showed us'. The end card's offer, cost line and URL are replaced by a spoken or super CTA such as 'Comment PËRGJIGJE and we'll send the 3-message reply script', 'Save this for your front desk' or 'Send this to the clinic owner who answers at midnight'. Keep the 35 to 45 s length, the cold-open pain line and the 6-word payoff; the series value comes from recurring hosts, since locked voices and one start frame per host make a weekly show possible.

story_structures.name: Three-person panel (host + problem guest + fix guest)
story_structures.shape: The host asks the questions (beats 2, 5, 9); guest 1 carries the problem beats (1, 3, 7); guest 2 carries the cause, failed fix, fix and payoff (4, 6, 8, 10)
story_structures.organic_fit: Works as an organic 'roundtable' episode for an agency: the agency strategist as host, a local business owner with the pain, and another owner who fixed it. It costs one more casting brief, reference photo, start frame and set of generations (line 114). Good for a recurring 'Biznes Talk' series format, with the CTA to follow for the next episode or comment a keyword for the checklist.

story_structures.name: Hook variants: main / new title bar / later start
story_structures.shape: V1: cold-open line 1 + title bar A; V2: same open + title bar B naming the ICP another way (a question or the accommodation in their words); V3: drop the first 1-2 turns and start on a later line that works cold (e.g. the aha line) + title bar C; no line ever plays twice
story_structures.organic_fit: Organic can't A/B test the way ads do, but V2 and V3 can run as Instagram trial reels or be reposted on other surfaces at no generation cost. V3 (open on the aha 'Whoever answers first gets them') is a strong organic hook for save-and-share. Re-run the seam tests on V3.

story_structures.name: Solo creator UGC across the buyer's day (section 13)
story_structures.shape: Line 1 cold-open pain to the phone camera in setting 1 → the accommodation and escalation as she moves through 1 to 3 real settings from her day (car, desk, bed at 11 pm) → the cause/aha → the failed fix → what changed (mechanism, product or service) → lived payoff; jump cuts between lines
story_structures.organic_fit: This is the closest match to the 'POV day in the life of the buyer with their pains, then the revelation of the mechanism' format: the settings come from the avatar's day and each carries a pain moment. For a B2B services client: a clinic or showroom owner's day (morning DMs unanswered in the car, a lost lead at the desk, WhatsApps in bed at 11 pm), then the reveal that speed of reply is the mechanism. Close on the payoff plus an organic CTA (comment keyword for the DM funnel, save, send). Script it in Script Lab with the UGC adapter (18d) at D30, C45 or S60, and drop the end card's offer and URL.

story_structures.name: Long cut conversation (L150, 2 to 3 min)
story_structures.shape: Loops problem → promise → mechanism → objection → proof, repeated; can carry a second guest story; covers more of the six objections in L13 order; written as its own script, never trimmed into the short one
story_structures.organic_fit: Fits organic as a longer Reel or a YouTube/Facebook video 'episode' where the agency teaches. Each loop can be cut into a standalone 30 to 45 s clip if each is written with its own cold open. Needs a stated reason under Script Lab rules; for organic, the reason is 'education / series episode'.

Framing for organic surfaces: keep captions out of the Reels UI zone (the skill gives no % safe zone, only 'lower middle'). The 'letterboxed 16:9 inside 9:16' native crop (line 458) needs an explicit step, because the ffmpeg recipe only scales to 1080x1920.
visual_qa_overlap:
What the skill already does. (1) Reference stage: numbered Pinterest contact sheets of about 12, each candidate scored 0-2 on 8 checks, keep 13 or more out of 16, a reject-on-sight list, and a reference board log. (2) Frame stage (5.4): 8 checks at full size: same person (start frame next to its master-frame crop), one image per person, likeness (master faces vs Pinterest faces), skin, hands and five fingers, props, light and no logos, characters distinct, real-podcast look at phone size, and gaze/expression/hands plus title-bar clearance. Retake with one fix; drift twice means using the upscaled crop. (3) Frame plan F0..F2 as a structural check (images = hosts + 1). (4) Prompt: a fixed template (section 8) with a tone table and a behaviour lock, but no prompt review step. 'Every prompt follows the hub G1 prompt card' is asserted, not checked, and the podcast template actually diverges from the G1 card (1 shot vs 2-4, static tripod vs handheld micro-shake, no background people vs 2-3 named background people). (5) Takes: a take sheet per clip with a frame every 1 s plus the first and last 0.1 s, face crops at least 190 px, a 6-item reject list (lens look, looking down or eyes closed over 1 s, gestures, smiling on a problem line, frozen over 4 s, drift from the start frame), a pitch check within 1.5 semitones, and a drift check (2 s windows every 0.25 s). (6) Final: a frame sheet every 1.5 s or less plus every cut boundary, caption-face match, pose snaps, title bar over a head, final transcript, pitch, loudness and gap tables, a hook check and a conversation check. There are no storyboards in this format: the frame plan replaces them. All of these reviews are self-reviews by the generating agent. The only fresh-agent check in the chain is Script Lab's cold read of the script.

What a fresh-agent reviewer set would replace or add. A Visual Reviewer, given only the casting cards, Pinterest picks and generated frames, would take over the 5.4 frame QA and the likeness check: the generator is biased toward passing its own frames, and the likeness 'would a stranger say it's the same person' test needs a stranger. It would also check the master-frame crop against the start frame, and, added, the title bar plus AI tag layout at the top. A Prompt Reviewer would lint every clip prompt before spend against a podcast-specific card: exactly 1 image + 1 audio, minimax_h3 / 2K / 9:16, declined_preset_id value present, duration = stem length within 5-15 s, one continuous shot, static camera, no gesture verbs outside the behaviour lock, tone of 5 words or fewer and softened, a laugh only when the script has '(small laugh)', numbers as words, the listening-beat times matching the stem map, and no Pinterest attachment. A Take Reviewer would read each take sheet blind against the 9.3 reject list and the drift table, deciding retakes per used line. A Final Reviewer would read the rendered-file sheet for caption-on-wrong-face, pose snaps and reaction-shot cadence (one every 10 s or less). Shared needs to add: a labelled frame-sheet tiler (crop size 190 px or more), pitch, loudness and gap table scripts (none exist locally), and a machine-readable record of each verdict.
